declared.title: Vanishing time in the pursuit of happiness
declared.foundIn: OpenAlex search « pursuit of happiness can be lonely » (2026-11-22)

population: one survey and three experiments; samples and countries not given in the abstract

findings.text: Seeking happiness, measured or induced, made people feel they had less time

support.sentence: Four studies demonstrated that trait-level happiness seeking (Study 1) as well as direct manipulation of happiness seeking (Studies 2, 3, and 4) consistently reveal the same pattern: reduced feelings of time availability while pursuing happiness.

findings.text: In one experiment, pursuing happiness lowered happiness, partly by making time feel scarce

support.sentence: In addition, pursuing happiness can ultimately decrease happiness, in part, by reducing perceptions of time availability (Study 4), extending theories on happiness, goal pursuit, and perceptions of time.

limits: the drop in happiness rests on one study (Study 4)
sample sizes and countries not given in the abstract (abstract only)
brief inductions in the lab or online, effect measured right after
